text.headline: Timeline of Suriname
text.text: Major events in the history of Suriname.

events.headline: First European Contact
events.text: Spanish explorers reach the Suriname coast, encountering indigenous Arawak and Carib peoples.

events.headline: British Settlement Established
events.text: English colonists establish sugar plantations worked by enslaved Africans.

events.headline: Dutch Take Control
events.text: The Dutch seize Suriname from the British, trading it for New Amsterdam (modern New York).

events.headline: Maroons Resist Slavery
events.text: Escaped slaves form independent communities in the interior, fighting for freedom and autonomy.

events.headline: Abolition of Slavery
events.text: Slavery is abolished, but indentured laborers from India and Java replace enslaved workers.

events.headline: Autonomous Status Within the Kingdom of the Netherlands
events.text: Suriname gains internal self-government while remaining under Dutch sovereignty.

events.headline: Independence from the Netherlands
events.text: Suriname becomes an independent republic with Paramaribo as its capital.

events.headline: Military Coup
events.text: Sergeant Dési Bouterse leads a coup, suspending the constitution and ruling by decree.

events.headline: Economic and Environmental Challenges
events.text: Suriname faces debt and deforestation concerns while pursuing sustainable development.
